question: NPC: A class, an object, and self
intro: I'm Zoya, the Golem-Shaper. This chapter takes classes and objects further than you have taken them before. But first, a quick check of the words you already know.

steps.say: A **class** is a design. Here is one. It says that every Golem stores two **attributes**, `name` and `power`, and has a **method**, `lift`.

beats.say: A **class** is a design. Here is one.
beats.narrate: A class is a design. It isn't a thing itself. It describes what each thing built from it will have. Here's one.
Here's the class Golem. Notice the two lines that begin with self dot, inside the init method, and then a second method, lift, at the bottom.

beats.say: It says that every Golem stores two **attributes**, `name` and `power`, and has a **method**, `lift`.
beats.narrate: So every Golem stores two attributes, its name and its power: those are the lines with self dot. And every Golem has a method, lift, that it can run.

steps.say: Calling the class builds an **object** and runs its setup method, `__init__`, on it. **self** is the object being worked on, so each golem stores its own name and its own power.

beats.narrate: Now two golems are built from that one class: clay, with a power of 3, and iron, with a power of 9. The last line calls lift on iron.

beats.say: Calling the class builds an **object** and runs its setup method, `__init__`, on it. **self** is the object being worked on, so each golem stores its own name and its own power.
beats.narrate: Calling the class builds an object, and then runs its setup method, the init method, on that new object. Self is the object being worked on. Here, that's the new golem being set up. So each golem stores its own name and its own power, inside its own object.

figure.alt: Two variables, clay and iron, each pointing at its own Golem object. The first object stores name Clay and power 3; the second stores name Iron and power 9.
figure.caption: Two objects from one class.

beats.narrate: In the picture, follow each blue arrow from a name to its object. The name clay leads to one Golem, with power 3. The name iron leads to a different Golem, with power 9.

check.why: The call is made on `iron`, so inside `lift`, `self` is `iron`: `self.name` is `"Iron"` and `self.power` is 9.
check.narrate: So, when the last line calls lift on iron, what does it return?
check.why_narrate: The call is made on iron, so inside lift, self is iron. Self dot name is Iron, and self dot power is 9. So lift returns Iron lifts 9.

steps.say: Four words to carry forward. A class is the design. An object, also called an **instance**, is one thing built from it. An attribute is a value an object stores. A method is a function that belongs to the class. Everything today is built from those four.

beats.say: Four words to carry forward. A class is the design. An object, also called an **instance**, is one thing built from it.
beats.narrate: Here are four words to carry forward. A class is the design. An object, which you'll also hear called an instance, is one thing built from that design.

beats.say: An attribute is a value an object stores. A method is a function that belongs to the class. Everything today is built from those four.
beats.narrate: An attribute is a value an object stores, like a golem's power. A method is a function that belongs to the class, like lift. Everything in this chapter is built from those four words.

outro: Show me you still have it.
intro_narrate: I'm Zoya, the Golem-Shaper. In this chapter, we'll take classes and objects further than you've taken them before. But first, let's have a quick check of the words you already know, so that we're sure of them. It won't take long.
outro_narrate: Now it's your turn. Show me you still have all of it.

question: Two objects are built from one class. What does the program print?
code:
class Golem:
    def __init__(self, name, power):
        self.name = name
        self.power = power

    def boost(self):
        self.power = self.power + 2

a = Golem("Ash", 4)
b = Golem("Bog", 7)
a.boost()
a.boost()
print(a.power, b.power)
feedback: boost was called twice on a and never on b. Each object has its own power, so a goes from 4 to 8 while b stays at 7.

question: Match each object-oriented term to its meaning.

pairs.definition: A design that objects are built from
One object built from a class
A value that an object stores
A function that belongs to a class
The setup code run on each new object

feedback: A class is the design; an instance (an object) is one thing built from it. Attributes are what an object knows, methods are what it can do, and __init__ gives a new object its starting attributes.

question: Inside a method, what is self?
correct: The one object that the method was called on
incorrect: The class that the method is written inside of
A copy of the object, thrown away afterwards
The first value typed inside the parentheses
feedback: In iron.lift(), self is iron. It is the real object, not a copy, which is why self.power = ... changes that object for good. Python passes it in for you; you never type it in the call.

question: The __init__ of a class named Golem stores {{k}} attributes on self. A program builds {{n}} Golem objects. How many attribute values are being stored altogether?
feedback_template: Every object gets its own set of attributes, so {{n}} objects with {{k}} attributes each store {{expected}} values. The class is written once; the data is kept once per object.

question: NPC: An object inside an object
intro: An attribute can hold a number or a string. It can also hold something more interesting.

steps.say: Look at Hero's `weapon` attribute: it is meant to hold a whole Weapon object. So a Hero **has a** Weapon. Building a class out of other objects like this is called **composition**.

feedback: Inside strike, self is the hero. self.weapon is her Weapon object, and self.weapon.damage is 5, so strike returns 10.

feedback: The loop visits each Item in the pack's list and asks it for its weight: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12. It is the accumulator pattern, with objects in the list instead of numbers.

feedback: Only one Weapon was ever built. Both heroes store a reference to that same object, so a change made through a is seen through b. It is the aliasing you met with lists, now with objects.

question: NPC: A child class starts with everything
intro: Sometimes a new class needs everything an existing class already has, plus a little more. You should not have to write all of that again.

steps.say: The parentheses in `class Wolf(Creature):` name a parent. Wolf is a **child class**, or subclass, of Creature. Creature is its **parent class**, or superclass. Wolf writes only `howl`, yet a Wolf starts with everything a Creature has: `__init__` and `describe` too. That is **inheritance**.

In every class, from the top of the file
